title: Television: Ringo Starr on VH1 Storytellers | 1998
content:
Ringo Starr recorded an edition of VH1 Storytellers on 13 May 1998.

The recording took place at Sony Music Studios in Manhattan, New York City, in front of an invited audience which included the teen group Hanson.

Starr’s band was The Roundheads:

Joe Walsh: guitar, vocals
Mark Hudson: guitar, harmonica, vocals
Gary Burr: guitar, mandolin, vocals
Steve Dudas: guitar
Jack Blades: bass guitar, vocals
Jim Cox: keyboards, vocals
Scott Gordon: harmonica
Simon Kirke: drums, percussion

This was one of a handful of shows by Starr and The Roundheads, in support of the Vertical Man album. They performed twelve songs:

  • ‘With A Little Help From My Friends’
  • ‘It Don’t Come Easy’
  • ‘I Was Walkin”
  • ‘Don’t Pass Me By’
  • ‘Back Off Boogaloo’
  • ‘King Of Broken Hearts’
  • ‘Octopus’s Garden’
  • ‘Photograph’
  • ‘La De Da’
  • ‘What In The… World’
  • ‘Love Me Do’
  • ‘With A Little Help From My Friends’ (Reprise)

The 45-minute edition of VH1 Storytellers was first broadcast in the US on VH1 on 28 June 1998, and in Europe on 8 November.

The audio was mixed at Westlake Studios and Blue House Studios in Los Angeles by Scott Gordon and Mark Hudson, and the VH1 Storytellers album was released on 20 October 1998. It was Starr’s first live album without the All-Starr Band.

Sony Music Studios was a music and broadcasting complex situated at 460 W 54th Street, in the Hell’s Kitchen district of Manhattan. It opened in 1993 and closed in August 2007.
